title: AFLiP: An Access-Recomputation Decoupling Framework for Efficient and Structure-Preserving GNN-based Link Prediction

problem.claim: Neighborhood expansion makes edge-level mini-batches approach near full-graph computation, weakening the benefit of shared message-passing encoders.

gap.claim: Existing scalable techniques make recomputation decisions implicitly through structural access, either recomputing all accessed nodes or only target nodes in a batch.

contributions.claim: Access-Decoupled Recomputation treats recomputation as an explicit optimization decision while preserving the original graph structure without neighborhood sampling.
AFLiP realizes Access-Decoupled Recomputation as an efficient, structure-preserving framework for GNN-based link prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across varied models and datasets, AFLiP attains accuracy at least as high as full recomputation, whereas sampling and static reuse degrade results in a dataset-dependent manner.
Compared with full recomputation, AFLiP reaches the best checkpoint up to 3.1× faster and scales to web-scale graphs where full recomputation is infeasible.
AFLiP achieves up to 16× higher throughput than sampling on Friendster.

narrative_sequence.summary: Shared message-passing encoders amortize node encoding across edges.
Neighborhood expansion reduces the computational benefit of edge-level mini-batches.
Existing scalable methods make recomputation decisions implicitly through structural access.
The paper introduces explicit access-decoupled recomputation and implements it in AFLiP without neighborhood sampling.
The authors report competitive accuracy, faster checkpoint attainment, web-scale applicability, and higher throughput than sampling.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates recomputation decisions from structural access while preserving the original graph structure.

interpretation.claim: Decoupling a computational policy from data-access structure may provide efficiency without requiring neighborhood sampling.

application.claim: This design may be applicable to graph-learning systems where neighborhood expansion makes mini-batch computation costly.

exception.claim: Reported degradation from sampling and static reuse is dataset-dependent.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the recomputation optimization objective or decision procedure.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated models and datasets beyond Friendster.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols, baselines, or variance estimates.
